docs.title: Ganderuka: Extended Rukwangali Technical Register
docs.text:
This platform is a dedicated, data-driven lexicographical project designed to scale Rukwangali (ISO 639-3: kwn) into a precise language capable of handling modern scientific research, advanced mathematics, software architecture, and industrial engineering.

Rather than relying on forced mechanical templates, this register maps technical domains through natural coining, contextual processing, and systematic etymology rooted securely within native morphosyntactic structures.

docs.title: 🏛️ System Scope
docs.text: Our work is actively divided into six specialized fields, mapped directly to their corresponding development tracks: * Muvaru (Mathematics) * Ediwomutji (Chemistry) * Ediwonsitwe (Physics) * Yokompiuta (Computing) * Upangerera (Engineering) * Ediwomwenyo (Biology)

docs.title: 🎯 Implementation Objectives
docs.text:
1. Academic Localization: Creating foundational learning guides and textbook schemas to support high-level education.
  2. Computational Portability: Maintaining strict machine-readable arrays (.typ, .json) so developers can easily integrate these terms into translation engines, localized software applications, and web tools.
  3. Open Access: Preserving the open-source freedom of this linguistic data so anyone can build on top of it without restriction.

docs.text: This system is strictly protected under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0) license. Plagiarism, uncredited reproduction, or locking this data behind proprietary closed paywalls is legally prohibited.

docs.title: Mathematics Technical Register
docs.text: Term (EN) Extended Rukwangali Pos Definition (EN / RK) Formula / Notes Even Number nomora zokuhetakana n. EN: an integer that is exactly divisible by 2 without leaving a remainder (n = 2k)RK: Nomora zokuvura kugaununa pauvali pwahana yihupo (n = 2k).Example: 2 no 4 no 6 kwahama mo nonomora dokuhetakana. — 2, 4, and 6 belong to even numbers. Class 9/10 (nomora zokuhetakana / ). Formed from nomora + associative modifier derived from -hetakana (to balance, pair, align evenly). Directly opposes nomora depando (odd numbers, $2k + 1$). Plural: nonomora dokuhetakana
